original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Replace the fractional idle relaxation in the selected complex word's packing ceiling with the attained optimum over integer idle histograms, and certify the tighter ceiling that follows. Then re-price the centre-free lever row, whose premises also admit integer counts.
scope_change_reason: The card's acceptance gate is to screen a candidate per-call local profile with ceiling.ceiling() and to read the lever table before choosing a target. The screening tool that the card points at returns a ceiling derived from a fractional idle histogram (1646/51 rank-51 children), so its headroom figure is optimistic by an unquantified amount, and its only integer control is 25 sampled histograms. This package first repairs that shared instrument: it computes the attained integer optimum, certifies the tighter ceiling, and re-prices one lever row. No candidate profile is synthesized and no supplier is proposed, so the card's construction question is untouched; only the budget those candidates would be screened against is corrected.
bottleneck_link: The complex side binds, and the family's diagnosis says packing of the selected word has under 0.87% headroom. That figure is a fractional relaxation, so the reachable headroom is smaller: this package measures the exact residual at +0.783% and shows a target-scale gain needs about 95% less local excess spend or a changed coverage law, not better packing.
stop_rule: Stop after the selected word's integer ceiling, one lever row and the two-unpaid premise's integrality. Do not extract idle histograms for pending local words, and do not launch a per-word ceiling census in this session.
evidence: RESULT.json: attained optimum {rank 51: 32, rank 14: 1} per call; integer ceiling 0.00168860344652699995 against the relaxation's 0.00169005410908900006; kappa upper bound 0.00168575687166350251 against 0.0016872026453254019; max gain over the selected kappa 0.782985% against 0.86942%, so integrality removes 0.0864 percentage points of headroom; bracket witnessed on both sides; 13 recorded controls. The centre-free lever row moves from 0.00471531 to 0.00471129 kappa cap. The two-unpaid premise has non-integral per-call idle mass 13918/9.

open_questions.question: What is the exact integer ceiling of each pending local word (#1148/#1169/#1218 lineage), and is its per-call idle mass even integral?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It separates packing headroom from local-word gains in the review queue, and a non-integral idle mass means a published figure is relaxation-only.
open_questions.first_step: Extract each claim's per-call idle mass, run integrality.ceiling_int on its local profile, and report the relaxation/integer pair side by side.
open_questions.blocked_by: Each claim's idle histogram is inside its own package; the same blocker the parent package records.

open_questions.question: How does the integer/fractional ceiling ratio depend on the idle mass modulo the guard cap R?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The correction here is set by 1646 mod 51 = 14, the rank the fractional remainder must land on. Knowing whether 0.086 percentage points is typical or an outlier tells a proposer how much of a quoted headroom is real.
open_questions.first_step: For fixed R, sweep the idle mass M over a full period and record ceil_int/ceil_relax, isolating the effect of M mod R from the effect of M.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing beyond this package: it is a sweep over the same pinned model. It is not attempted here only because the session stopped at the selected word.
